source_refs.note: Antiviral and antiretroviral drugs with the book's box (PDF 212).

blocks.text: Antiviral drugs treat viral infections. They prevent the growth and multiplication of viruses within the body and can combat a wide range of viruses, including the hepatitis, influenza and herpes viruses.

Antiretroviral drugs treat illnesses caused by retroviruses, including HIV (human immunodeficiency virus). They help the immune system's defence and stop HIV from multiplying. Retroviruses are viruses with RNA as their genetic material that replicate using the enzyme reverse transcriptase.

blocks.title: Book's box
blocks.text: All antiretrovirals are antivirals, but all antivirals are not antiretrovirals.

blocks.prompt: Differentiate between antiviral and antiretroviral drugs.
blocks.explanation: Antivirals act against viruses in general (such as hepatitis, influenza and herpes); antiretrovirals act specifically against retroviruses such as HIV, which use reverse transcriptase.

items: Antiretrovirals: HIV and other retroviruses (RNA genome, reverse transcriptase).
